answer: Latency triangulation ties each agent seat to a place. Every epoch, five randomly drawn verifiers on different continents send signed fresh nonces, and light-speed round trips locate the seat within about 300 km. A farm of a thousand clones on one jade-coloured server shows a single location and identical jitter, so those seats share one reward. Relays only add delay, and nothing like a drifting dune helps, since old replies fail the fresh nonce. Every real extra seat needs its own host in another region, near $10 a month, giving marble-solid proof that a clone farm costs more than it earns.
